balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

productMix.title: Revenue by product line
productMix.content:
Lonking reports five machinery product categories: wheel loaders, forklifts, excavators, road rollers and components & other.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: wheel loaders (~43% of FY2025 revenue) are the legacy cash-cow line and forklifts (~31%) the second pillar, but excavators (~15%) is the fastest-growing category -- revenue roughly doubled from RMB1,055.6m in FY2024 to RMB1,690.2m in FY2025 -- as Lonking pushes into a segment historically dominated by larger rivals.

What to watch:

  • Whether excavator growth continues or was a one-off restocking cycle
  • Wheel-loader revenue, which tracks China property/infrastructure construction activity most directly
  • Components & other as a stable base versus the cyclical machine lines

exportMix.title: Revenue outside mainland China
exportMix.content:
The share of revenue earned outside mainland China -- exports and overseas subsidiaries -- only disclosed in half-year filings.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: management calls overseas expansion a growth driver as the domestic construction-machinery market matures; the export share rose from RMB1,467.3m (H1 FY2024) to RMB1,979.4m (H1 FY2026) against a domestic market exposed to China property-sector weakness.

What to watch:

  • Export revenue growing faster than domestic revenue
  • Full-year rows are blank by nature -- only H1/H2 filings disclose the split
  • Whether export growth offsets softness in the mainland infrastructure cycle

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Lonking Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: The first build (base IV HK$6.54, +134% at a price in the upper 77% of its 10-year range) tripped scripts/sanity_check.py with diagnosis growth_too_high: the base 10-year revenue CAGR of 4.7% exceeded the FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle CAGR of 2.8%. Fix applied per the runbook (Step 8c.5, items 3 and 4): (1) base growth path capped at a 2.77% 10-year CAGR, keeping the banked FY2026 +15% and flattening to 1% by FY2032, terminal growth 2.5% -> 2.0%; bull trimmed 6.4% -> 5.0% for ordering; bear unchanged (~0%). (2) Exit-multiple caps set from the stock's own 10-year EV/EBITDA range -- bear 3.7x (min), base 6.6x (average), bull 10.9x (max) -- expressed as owner-FCF cap multiples of 5.6x / 9.5x / 14x (bull kept at the tighter 14x already judged). Margins, capex, D&A, tax, working capital, WACC, bridge and weights were deliberately left unchanged. The residual upside after the fix (base IV HK$5.68, +103%) is almost entirely the cash: Lonking holds RMB7,276.6m of cash/time deposits plus RMB900.8m of FVTPL investments against zero borrowings (net of the FY2025 dividend paid 31 July 2026, about HK$2.04/share, ~73% of the share price), and the 10-year historical multiples this check compares against were struck on an enterprise value that already deducted that cash. Crediting the cash at face is the house's deliberate choice, charged through a 25% bear weight and historical-range exit multiples for the operating business rather than through an ad-hoc discount on the cash -- a multi-bagger case built on a cash floor plus a modest, through-cycle operating recovery, not on a re-rating of the machinery business.
